company_name: Shell plc (NYSE ADR, 1 ADS = 2 ordinary shares)

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average ordinary shares for Q2 2026 (5,637.0m, H1-2026 interim EPS note) divided by the ADS ratio of 2, so every per-share output is per NYSE ADS and comparable to current_price. Held FLAT: SBC ($774m, 0.29% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Shell's actual count is FALLING ~3-4%/yr because buybacks ($13.9bn FY2025, $6.2bn H1 2026) dwarf SBC; the flat convention is therefore conservative. Pro forma for the ARC Resources acquisition (COMPLETED 2 September 2026, after the 2026-06-30 balance-sheet date; the Q3 2026 results will carry the first post-deal balance sheet and are the natural trigger for refreshing these anchors): c.+229m ordinary shares (+c.114m ADS, ~4%) and c.+$4.4bn net debt (C$8.20/share cash consideration ~$3.4bn plus ARC's own net debt); the deal is treated as value-neutral at the price paid (~7x EBITDA, in line with Shell's own multiple), so per-ADS value is unchanged and the pre-deal anchors are kept.
inputs.interest_income_note: Shell holds $31.4bn cash but is a net-debt company (net debt ex leases $12.1bn; $41.8bn on Shell's lease-inclusive definition). Interest income (~$2.0bn FY2025, falling with lower cash and rates) sits outside Adjusted EBITDA (which is before net interest), so it is not inside the flows and there is nothing to strip; net debt is deducted as gross debt less cash in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F Note 28 'Share-based compensation expense', equity-settled $774m (2024 $732m, 2023 $700m); matches Metrics.csv StockBasedComp. Shell discloses no separate net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $13,879m; H1 2026 $6,183m. A $3.0bn + $1.2bn catch-up programme runs to the Q3 2026 results. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (count held flat, SBC expensed).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation date is the following Sunday)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC: 10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 -> cost of equity ~9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (fair value of debt ex leases below carrying value), after-tax ~3.75%; weights ~85% equity / 15% debt on market cap ~$269bn vs debt ex leases $43.4bn -> ~8.2%, rounded UP to 8.5% for an integrated commodity producer. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the Middle East conflict and transition risk are charged ONCE, in the probability-weighted driver paths, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. The full IFRS 16 lease cash outflow (FY2025 $7,127m = $5,261m principal + $1,866m interest, 20-F Note 22) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (2.6-2.8% of revenue), and lease liabilities ($29,627m at 2026-06-30 = total debt $73,076m less debt ex leases $43,449m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Consistently, D&A for the cash-tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 ROU charge $5,600m) and ex impairments ($3,133m net): 22,167 - 5,600 = $16,567m = 6.2% of revenue. Shell's Adjusted EBITDA is post-IFRS 16, so the lease charge is not double-counted in the margin. Lease-consistent multiple: EV ex leases / (Adj EBITDA less lease cash).
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows include the small non-controlling-interest share (NCI book $995m at 2026-06-30, attributable income ~$0.1-0.4bn/yr); the NCI book value is deducted once in equity_bridge. Not charged in the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical'), built on MID-CYCLE commodity assumptions per owner-fcf-adaptations.md section (f) and the HAL precedent -- not on the Q2 2026 spike. CYCLE POSITION: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was $20.7bn (vs $13-14bn/quarter in 2025) on 'higher realised prices' and LNG trading gains caused by the Middle East conflict (which also cut Qatari volumes); the stock sits near its 52-week high. FY2025 (Brent ~$68, weak chemicals and trading, Adj EBITDA $56.1bn = 21.0% margin vs 21.0/22.1/21.6/23.1% in FY2021-24) is taken as a slightly-below-mid-cycle anchor; base margins recover to 22.5% (pre-SBC) by year 4 on the $5-7bn structural cost programme ($5.1bn delivered by end-2025) and LNG Canada/Pavilion volumes. TIMING: the balance sheet (net debt, shares) is anchored at 2026-06-30, so the H1 2026 windfall (Shell-defined FCF $20.5bn, net debt down $3.9bn from Dec-25 after $10.6bn of distributions) is captured in net debt and NOT again in year 1; forecast year 1 is the twelve months from the balance-sheet date, discounted end-of-year. CAPEX: Shell's 'cash capital expenditure' definition ($20,915m FY2025) INCLUDES investments in joint ventures/associates ($1,886m) because JV dividends ($2.6bn) are inside CFFO; the 20-F CFS 'Capital expenditure' line is $18,947m. FY2026 cash capex guidance was lifted to $24-26bn from the CMD $20-22bn p.a. 2025-28 frame; the difference is read as the ARC cash consideration (~$3.4bn), so underlying capex stays ~7.6-7.8% of revenue. CASH TAX: 36% of unlevered post-lease EBIT reproduces FY2025 cash tax paid ($11,638m on $32,441m); reported effective rate is 39-45% on a post-interest, post-impairment base. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture 0 -- Shell's WC swings are price-driven (FY2023 +7.1bn, FY2024 +2.1bn, FY2025 -1.8bn) and net to ~zero through the cycle; growth here is mostly nominal/volume so no structural build is modelled. OWNER FCF: last_fcf keeps the contract identity (reported FCF 23,916 - SBC 774 - interest income 0 = 23,142); the engine's year-1 FCF (~$17.4bn) is lower because lease cash ($7.1bn) and JV investments ($1.9bn) are charged inside the component build -- see last_fcf_post_lease_and_jv_capex (16,414 FY2025, ties to CFFO ex-WC 44,666 - leases 7,127 - cash capex 20,915 = 16,624). POST-BALANCE-SHEET ITEMS: ARC Resources closed 2026-09-02 (value-neutral, see share_count_basis; refresh shares and net debt from the Q3 2026 results); LNG Canada Phase 2 FID (Sept 2026) sits inside the $20-22bn 2027-28 cash capex frame per the Analysis JSON; Jiffy Lube $1.3bn sale completed 2026-06-30 (in the balance sheet); Na Kika $1.7bn and Sprng Energy $1.8bn disposals pending (their flows are inside the base and the proceeds roughly equal the value given up; ignored). SANITY-CHECK FLAG for the orchestrator: shares_outstanding is in ADS units (2,818.5m) while Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding and EPS are per ORDINARY share (5,637m; FY2025 EPS $3.00 = $6.00/ADS) -- sanity_check.py has a known ADS-denomination bug (MEMORY: divides per-ADS price by per-common metrics), so P/E and P/B printed off the CSV will be 2x too high.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest at book (deducted once; flows are consolidated)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle volume growth (LNG Canada ramp, Pavilion, ARC) at flat real commodity prices; the historical CAGRs are cycle artefacts (FY2022 Brent ~$100 peak, FY2020 COVID trough) and are not used
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.9% 3yr / +2.3% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs; equity shrinks because distributions ($22.4bn FY2025) exceed earnings ($17.8bn), not because the business is shrinking. FCF CAGRs: 3yr -19.9% from the FY2022 peak, 5yr +6.2% from the FY2020 trough -- both endpoints are cycle extremes. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 EPS -2.78).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC: FY2020 17,161; FY2022 45,006; FY2025 23,142). SBC-adjusted and reported CAGRs are within 0.4pp of each other because SBC is ~0.3% of revenue -- SBC is not where Shell's cash goes.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle: Brent ~$65-70, LNG spreads normalise as the conflict premium fades, chemicals stay weak but refining is mid-cycle. Revenue +2% y1-2 (LNG Canada ramp, Pavilion volumes) fading to 1% nominal; EBITDA margin (pre-SBC) 21.6% -> 22.5% as the $5-7bn cost programme completes (FY2021-25 range 21.0-23.4%). Cash capex $21.2bn y1 within the $20-22bn frame, drifting to 7.6% of revenue. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF binds (Gordon at 8.5%/1.0% would be 13.5x).

bull.narrative: Sustained tightness: Brent $80+ and elevated LNG spreads persist beyond 2026 as Middle East supply (incl. Qatar) stays disrupted; Shell's LNG trading book and Integrated Gas capture the spread; the full $7bn cost target lands and ARC/LNG Canada add low-cost gas. Revenue +9% y1 then 1.5-3%; margin 22.8% -> 24.0% (above FY2024's 23.4%). Higher upstream share lifts cash tax to 38%. Terminal cap 13x.

bear.narrative: Conflict premium unwinds into oversupply: Brent ~$55 as OPEC+ volumes return and demand plateaus early; the 2027-28 LNG supply wave (Qatar North Field East, US Gulf) compresses spreads; chemicals and European refining stay loss-making; UK EPL-style windfall taxes recur. Revenue -8%/-3% then flat; margin 19.5% -> 20.5% (above the FY2020 COVID trough, below FY2021). Fixed vessel charters (2.8% of a smaller revenue) and D&A (6.6%) weigh; capex cut to ~$19bn. Nigeria litigation and ARC-funded gearing are the balance-sheet overhangs on this path. Zero terminal growth, 11x cap.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle Brent $65-70 with LNG spreads normalising; EBITDA margin recovers from FY2025's 21.3% (pre-SBC) to 22.5% as the structural cost programme completes; cash capex held at $20-22bn; terminal cap 12x binds. The H1 2026 windfall is in the 30 June 2026 net debt, not in the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Brent $80+ and elevated LNG spreads persist as Middle East supply stays disrupted; Shell's trading and Integrated Gas businesses capture the spread; margin 24% by year 5 and 13x terminal cap. Needs the conflict premium to outlast the 2027-28 LNG supply wave.
scenario_narratives.bear: Premium unwinds into oversupply: Brent ~$55, LNG spreads compressed by Qatar/US Gulf volumes, chemicals and European refining loss-making, windfall taxes; margin 19.5-20.5%, revenue 8-11% lower, zero terminal growth, 11x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Cyclical weighting 25/50/25 (HAL precedent), not the 15/50/35 house default: the bull case requires the conflict-driven price premium to outlast the 2027-28 LNG supply wave, which is a bet on geopolitics rather than on Shell, so bull is cut to 25%; bear is raised to 25% because the price sits near a 52-week high set on a Q2 2026 earnings spike and the downside path (oversupply plus windfall taxes) has precedent in 2015-16 and 2020. No solvency risk (gearing 18.7%, debt ex leases at fair value below book), so bear is not raised further.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Shell as a through-cycle cash generator, not on the FY2026 spike: owner FCF after leases, SBC and JV investment, at a 36% cash tax rate and a $20-22bn capex frame, capitalised at a cyclical cap of 11-13x. Shell's own CMD targets (FCF/share growth, 40-50% of CFFO distributed, $5-7bn structural cost cuts) are reflected only to the extent the FY2021-25 record supports them. Buybacks are value-neutral; the model's flat ADS count is conservative against a count actually falling 3-4%/yr.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity reversal: the Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $20.7bn and the 52-week high rest on a Middle East conflict price premium; a return to $60-65 Brent is the base case, not a risk, but the market price may be discounting the spike persisting.
LNG supply wave 2027-28 (Qatar North Field expansion, US Gulf Coast) compressing the spreads that drive Integrated Gas (~40% of Adjusted EBITDA).
Windfall and transition taxation: UK Energy Profits Levy precedents; cash tax rate assumed 36% of unlevered EBIT.
Capex creep: FY2026 cash capex guidance of $24-26bn vs the $20-22bn frame; the model assumes the excess is the ARC consideration.
ARC Resources integration (closed 2 Sept 2026): ~4% share issuance and ~$4.4bn net debt assumed value-neutral; pre-deal anchors until the Q3 2026 balance sheet is filed.

Nigeria litigation (Alame & Ors v Shell): the 10 Sept 2026 High Court ruling broadened potential liability to regional pollution ahead of a March 2027 trial -- an unquantified contingent liability not in the bridge.
LNG Canada Phase 2 FID (Sept 2026): megaproject cost/schedule risk inside the capex frame.

Lease-heavy structure: $29.6bn of IFRS 16 liabilities (LNG carriers, FPSOs, retail) charged as $7.1bn/yr operating cost; a lease-as-debt treatment would give a similar value but a different net-debt figure.
Energy-transition demand plateau: terminal growth 0-1.5% nominal and a terminal cap, not a perpetuity at GDP growth.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 68.63-99.16; price per NYSE ADS (2 ordinary shares).
data_sources.financials: FY2025 20-F (SEC HTML extract, SHEL_20F_FY2025.txt): key-metrics table (Adjusted EBITDA, cash capex, net debt), consolidated income statement, segment note (D&A ex impairments 22,167), Note 22 leases (cash outflow 7,127; ROU charge 5,600; lease liabilities 28,933), Note 28 SBC (774), tax note (effective rate 39%). Q2/H1 2026 interim (SHEL_Quarterly_H1-2026.txt): summary table, balance sheet at 2026-06-30, Note 6 debt ex leases 43,449, EPS note diluted shares 5,637.0m, Q3 2026 outlook, ARC Resources terms. Metrics.csv/duckdb kpis for CashTaxesPaid, ShareRepurchases, InterestIncome, DividendsPaid history.
data_sources.qualitative: SHEL_Analysis.json (landed mid-build): bull/bear cases, growth drivers (LNG Canada Phase 2 FID, ARC closed 2026-09-02, 2027-28 capex $20-22bn) and risks (Nigeria litigation ruling Sept 2026, chemicals/refining overcapacity, transition-strategy reversals); plus the FY2025 20-F strategy section, the Q2 2026 interim narrative and the 2025 Capital Markets Day targets.
